notes:
Summary: Aphelion is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a multi-region reserved GPU pool to serve low-latency chat + high-throughput embedding/rerank workloads. Primary ask: deterministic throughput guarantees with explicit failover headroom across two cloud regions (us-west-2, us-east-1) and cross-AZ distribution to tolerate AZ failures. They want an operator-grade SLA that ties latency SLOs (P95/P99) to credits and clear rules for capacity failover and warm standby.

Key quoted requirements: "p95 chat latency <= 150ms under typical load, p99 <= 400ms; sustained peak 40k QPS for embeddings during nightly batch windows; failover to secondary region within 90s with no more than 10% traffic loss" — CTO (A. Morales).

Capacity planning notes: Must provision reserved GPU pools with headroom for 1.5x baseline sustained traffic and separate burst pool for marketing spikes. Aphelion wants explicit per-region reservation (R1: 48 A100 equiv, R2: 24 A100 equiv) and the ability to borrow across regions with automated warm pool warming policies. Interested in a quantitative model from Redwood that maps GPUs -> effective QPS for their model family (mix of 3.7B/13B transformer variants) under multi-tenant packing assumptions.

SLA negotiation points: uptime SLA target 99.95% regional, plus runbook for cross-region failover. Credits asked: tiered credits (10% monthly invoice for p95 breach, 25% for p99) — Redwood legal wants to propose 5/15/30 tiered schedule instead. Also negotiating response time for incident escalation and on-call engineer routing for Dedicated customers.

Operational: They require VPC peering, KMS integration for key material, and audit logging export to their SIEM. Retention controls: customer cannot allow model logs to persist longer than 30 days by default. Data residency: EU data for EU-region training/embeddings only.

POC & POC Success Criteria: 2-week POC in us-west-2 with 24 reserved A100 equivalent, run defined throughput/latency tests and a failover drill to us-east-1. Success = p95 latency <= 160ms during sustained 80% load, failover drill completes <120s and data persistence validated, no data left in Redwood-managed logs beyond 7 days in POC mode.

Commercial asks: committed monthly spend with rollover credits for unused reserved GPU-hours, predictable burst pricing for short-term campaign spikes, and an option for annual true-up. Procurement shading: wants list of security artifacts (SOC2 Type II report, network diagrams) before legal approves the SAAS addendum.

Internal AE notes (shorthand):
- CTO hands-on, cares about predictable latency & cost math
- SE wants kernel-level perf numbers (per-model QPS tables) + quantization guidance from Optimize team
- CISO flagged KMS + retention + cross-region replication compliance
- Finance wants 12mo commit with quarterly review

Recommended Redwood asks: provide a region-by-region capacity model (CSV) mapping GPU counts to expected sustained QPS/p95/p99, run a 48h soak test, include warm-pool warming time metrics, and produce draft SLA with clear crediting and RTO/RPO for failover.

Stitched links: pricing deck in Drive, technical perf spreadsheet to attach in next email, Jira for capacity questions (RED-9832).
